title: Fingerprint identity resolution works within one tool's lineage and fails across tools
content:
Once identifiers are known to churn, the obvious repair is to fingerprint objects on stable attributes and resolve incoming identifiers onto a persistent internal id. Measured, this works extremely well in one direction and not at all in the other.

Across two consecutive weekly exports from the same tool, `(class, Name)` matched **1,690 of 1,690** objects — a complete recovery of identity that `GlobalId` comparison lost entirely. Across tools, the same fingerprint matched **0 of 1,690**: the design model and the 4D export of the same building shared no `(class, Name)` pair, because the 4D tool renames objects into its own scheme and flattens three real storeys into a single generated one under a synthetic site.

So identity resolution is per-lineage. Within a lineage, cheap attributes suffice. Across lineages, fingerprinting on names and classes cannot work at all, and any cross-tool join needs geometry, classification, or an explicit mapping maintained by someone.

Two design consequences. The spatial component of a fingerprint must be lineage-relative rather than absolute, since the hierarchy itself is not preserved. And a system holding identity across a whole project must model lineages explicitly, rather than assuming one global object namespace that the source tools demonstrably do not provide.
description: (class, Name) matched 100% across consecutive exports of one tool and 0% between two tools modelling the same building, because each renames objects and reshapes the spatial hierarchy.
